Any business serving alcohol in Douglas County is required to have license approval by the Local Liquor Licensing Authority . This includes new licenses, renewals, transfers and report of changes per the Colorado Liquor Code. Douglas County also approves all local tastings and special event permits. Fees vary based on the type of license needed.

License holders are responsible for complying with all laws, rules and regulations . Random compliance checks and inspections are performed by the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office and the Colorado Department of Revenue, Liquor Enforcement Division.

Transfer of a Liquor License

Any entity wishing to obtain an existing liquor license must complete a transfer of ownership. Transfers of ownership require both State and local approval but do not require a public hearing before the Local Liquor Licensing Authority. An applicant may also request a temporary permit for the period during which the transfer is being reviewed. Fees do apply.

Douglas County approves all local Tastings Permits. Retail liquor stores may conduct up to 104 tastings per year with dates that run concurrently with its license. No more than four tastings can be held in one week between the hours of 11 a.m. and 7 p.m. Any changes must be provided to Douglas County at least 72 hours in advance. Fees do apply.

New openings, closings, development, and community updates from Castle Rock, Parker, Highlands Ranch, Lone Tree, Castle Pines, and across Douglas County — first-person coverage you won't find anywhere else.

The former Pino’s space at 361 Village Square Lane is alive again. Castello Italiano — an upscale Italian restaurant from the family behind Farro Italian Restaurant — is officially open in Castle Pines, with wild boar ragu, bison short rib ravioli, and a 16-oz ribeye on the menu.

Castle Rock Town Council approved the site plan for a 100,054-square-foot King Soopers in Dawson Trails, with a pharmacy, a seven-pump fuel station and a 2027 opening. A Kroger representative told council The Ridge and Promenade are not closing.
Dollar Tree is building out a new store at 1970 E. County Line Road in The Plaza at Highlands Ranch — its second Highlands Ranch location. Hiring is already underway; no opening date yet.

Dunkin' announced its first Castle Rock restaurant, opening fall 2026 at 1185 Aloha Street in Founders Marketplace — a Next Generation store with a cold-drink tap system, a drive-thru, and a 4 a.m. daily open.
A locally owned pizzeria with an arcade is setting up in Suite 660 at the Outlets at Castle Rock. Peak Pizza announced itself this week — grand opening date still to come.

Life Time doesn't publish pricing for its Castle Pines club. A grand-opening breakdown shared publicly puts an individual membership at $329 a month and a family of five near $789. Here's that breakdown, and what's actually in the building.
The drive-thru coffee chain's Castle Pines building is up, the signage is installed and the lot is striped. The city's own development page still lists it as barely started.
Rock Bottom Restaurant & Brewery has closed its Highlands Ranch location along with Centennial, leaving Loveland as the chain's only remaining Colorado brewpub. The landlord is suing.

JP Cocina & Cantina opened Wednesday, August 19 in the old Wild Goose Saloon at 11160 S Pikes Peak Dr in Parker, from Jose Poblano of El Poblano Mexican Eats and The Perfect Time Cafe. Open 10am to midnight Sunday through Wednesday and 10am to 2am Thursday through Saturday, same menu all day. A happy hour is planned but hasn't started yet.
Egg Harbor Cafe Is Coming to Belleview Station in Denver

The family-owned breakfast brand that opened in Highlands Ranch this spring is expanding — a second Colorado location is coming to Belleview Station in southeast Denver, now aiming for a late-September opening.

Douglas County approved $7.5 million toward a 75,000-square-foot Gold Crown youth field house in Castle Rock's Dawson Trails — six basketball courts, a dozen volleyball courts, and an early-2028 opening.

105 West Brewing's all-inclusive Castle Rock Beer Fest Under the Stars returns Saturday, Sept 12, 2026, 4–9pm at the Philip S. Miller Park Amphitheater — 25+ Colorado breweries, 7+ food trucks, unlimited tastings, and live music. It sells out; no door sales.

The 24th Annual Taste of Douglas County returns Thursday, Aug 20, 2026, 5–8pm — an indoor, air-conditioned evening of food samples from dozens of area restaurants, drinks, and live entertainment at the Douglas County Events Center in Castle Rock. $10 in advance, $20 at the door.
GQue BBQ Coming to Parker — Taking Over the Former Freddy's Space

GQue BBQ, Colorado's championship-BBQ chain, is coming to Parker's Crown Point Center at 18424 Cottonwood Dr — the former Freddy's Frozen Custard & Steakburgers space. A Town of Parker permit describes the remodel. No opening date yet.
Shake Shack Opening in Parker August 12 — In the Former Wendy's Spot
Shake Shack is opening its first Parker location at 9185 Crown Crest Blvd on Wednesday, August 12, 2026 — in the space that formerly housed a Wendy's. Here's what we know.

A 31-acre, $400 million mixed-use district is under construction on Castle Rock's west side — a sports center, a hotel, six restaurants, and hundreds of homes, from the same developer behind Riverwalk downtown.

Salady — billed as South Korea's largest salad franchise, with 400-plus stores — opened in Parker on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at 9700 S Parker Rd in the Parker Gateway Marketplace. I went on opening day: here is the room, the menu, and what the bowls are actually like.

A new permanent sculpture called Big Drive — a bull, cow, and calf standing about 11 feet tall and 20 feet wide — is being installed at Castle Rock's Rock Park Open Space, where the Town's Western Heritage Cattle Drive begins each summer. Here's the story, the artists behind it, and the July 22 dedication.
Lost Canyon Ranch Open Space: I Hiked Every Open Trail. Here's the Guide.

Castle Rock's Lost Canyon Ranch Open Space opened July 13, 2026. I hiked all 10 miles over two days. Here is every open trail with real distance, elevation and shade, both trailheads, what is still closed, and what to know before you go. No dogs.
Pick N Tap: Indoor Pickleball, Golf, and a Restaurant Are Coming to Parker
The Town of Parker has approved Pick N Tap, a 19,960-square-foot restaurant with indoor pickleball courts and golf simulators at 11735 Disha Drive. Construction is expected to start soon.

The Southern fast-casual chain Chicken Salad Chick is finally underway in Castle Rock's Meadows neighborhood, near the movie theater and across from the hospitals. Dirt is moving on a location with a patio and drive-thru; an opening date hasn't been announced yet.

After 23 years in Castle Rock, world-championship magicians Carol Massie and Joe Givan have reopened as the Magic Manor — an intimate 90-seat magic theatre and event venue inside a historic 1908 Victorian property in Sedalia, the former Gabriel's Italian Restaurant.
24 Hour Fitness South Parker Closed for Renovation — Reopens July 11

The South Parker Super-Sport club at 11445 Twenty Mile Rd is temporarily closed for a targeted renovation and set to reopen July 11, 2026 — the same renovation 24 Hour Fitness just completed at its Castle Rock club. Expect the basketball court swapped out for an expanded free-weight area and turf zone, plus new equipment.
Black Rock Coffee Bar Now Open at Parker Road & Stroh Road
Black Rock Coffee Bar is now open at 6940 Stroh Rd (Parker Road & Stroh Road), opening Tuesday, June 30, 2026 — its third Parker location and 19th in Colorado, with a week of grand-opening specials.
Inside Emagine Parker: Opening Date, Photos & Prices

We toured Emagine Parker — Colorado's first Emagine theater, inside the former AMC Twenty Mile 10 — the night before it opened. Here's what it's actually like inside, with photos: 10 auditoriums, two EMX large-format screens, heated recliners, cuddle chairs, ticket prices, a full Colorado bar, and Little Dot Pizza.
The Groove Café Now Open at Lyric at RidgeGate in Lone Tree

The Groove — the new neighborhood hub at the Lyric at RidgeGate community in Lone Tree — is now open at 10930 Lyric Street, with a café serving coffee, breakfast, lunch, and dinner alongside a restaurant, welcome center, fitness area, and pool.

Denver-based Cerebral Brewing is opening its fourth taproom at 20117 East Mainstreet in downtown Parker. A 4,200-square-foot space inside the East Main development, with a roughly 2,000-square-foot patio, opens summer 2027.
Peaky Peak Coffee & Charcuterie — Lone Tree Concept Expanding to Denver and Parker

Peaky Peak Coffee & Charcuterie — Quy and Tracy Nguyen's Vietnamese-coffee-meets-charcuterie concept in Lone Tree — is expanding, with a second location in Denver's Golden Triangle and a third now confirmed for Parker's Mainstreet.

As 2026 gets underway, Littleton is changing in ways that feel noticeable but familiar. New storefronts are opening. Longtime businesses are moving to larger spaces. Construction is underway on projects that will shape how people shop, eat, and spend time in the city for years to come.

This isn’t growth for growth’s sake. Much of what’s happening is tied to everyday life: places to grab coffee, studios to work out, restaurants that fit into weekly routines, and retail that keeps people close to home. Some of these businesses are already open and settling in. Others are officially on the way, with buildouts and planning in progress. Together, they reflect a city growing with intention while holding onto what residents value most.
A Healthy Start: Fitness & Wellness Expansions

“New year, new me” feels especially fitting in Littleton, where staying active has long been part of daily life. From trail access and parks to walkable neighborhoods, fitness is already woven into the city’s culture. Heading into 2026, new studios and developments are adding indoor options that support that lifestyle year-round.

HAVN joins a deep roster of established fitness options throughout Littleton. Anytime Fitness offers flexible, no-frills gym access, while places like Camp MissFits focus on coached strength training and small-group formats. These spaces appeal to residents looking for structure, accountability, and personalized support.

Movement-based studios are also a big part of Littleton’s fitness culture. The Ballet Physique on Main Street blends barre, Pilates, and strength training in a boutique setting, while Pilates by Johanna and H2 Pilates Studio emphasize controlled, low-impact movement designed to support long-term mobility. Yoga remains a staple as well, with studios like Sumits Yoga Littleton offering classes that balance physical challenge with recovery and stress relief.

Community-centered options round out the picture. The Littleton Family YMCA and Douglas H. Buck Community Recreation Center continue to serve residents of all ages with group classes, open gym time, and accessible programming that keeps fitness inclusive.

Beyond individual studios, fitness is increasingly built into how Littleton grows. Mixed-use developments like Mineral Place are designed with trail access and on-site fitness amenities in mind, creating space for future wellness offerings that integrate naturally into daily routines. Together, these options reflect a city where staying active doesn’t require a single approach. It’s flexible and woven into everyday life.

Beyond Thai brings a fresh, modern take on Thai cuisine to Littleton, offering a menu that blends traditional flavors with contemporary presentation. Known for dishes like pad thai, curries, and noodle bowls, the restaurant provides a comfortable, sit-down dining experience that works for both casual nights out and special occasions. Its addition helps round out Littleton’s growing mix of global dining options.

Hearth Bakery & Coffee Shop expanded into Littleton in 2025 with a new location at 5610 S. Curtice Street. Known for its artisan breads, pastries, and comforting café fare, Hearth feels right at home on Main Street. Fresh-baked bread, hearty sandwiches, and a warm interior have made it a regular stop for breakfast, lunch, or a slower afternoon visit.

Hibachi V Express adds a fast-casual Japanese grill option to Littleton’s dining mix. Located in a former Pierogies shop, the restaurant serves hibachi-style meals like grilled steak, chicken, or shrimp with vegetables and rice, along with items such as okonomiyaki. It’s a convenient option for lunch or takeout without the time commitment of a traditional hibachi restaurant.

Craft beverage fans can also visit Honnibrook Craft Meadery , which opened a tasting room in Downtown Littleton. Often referred to as the “Mead Cottage,” the space on Rapp Street offers honey-based wines ranging from traditional styles to fruit-forward blends, providing a quieter alternative to beer and cocktails.

Littleton Brewing Company officially opened in March 2025, transforming a former autobody shop into a two-story neighborhood brewery. Family-owned and community-focused, the brewery features a rooftop patio with fire pits that draws steady crowds when the weather cooperates. With a well-rounded beer lineup that includes approachable lagers and hop-forward styles, it has quickly become a favorite gathering spot.

Dirt Coffee , a beloved hometown coffee shop known for its mission to empower neurodivergent individuals in the workforce, moved into a larger Downtown Littleton location in late 2025. The new space at 2506 W. Alamo Ave. includes an expanded café and Colorado’s first drop-in Workforce Connection Center for neurodivergent job seekers. The move allows Dirt Coffee to serve more customers, host events, and deepen its community impact while continuing to do what it does best.

Ruby Jane Boutique , a Colorado-based retailer known for mountain-chic fashion and gifts, opened a new store on Littleton’s Main Street. For many locals, it means no longer needing to head to Denver or mountain towns to shop the brand’s curated styles. Its arrival reflects a broader increase in downtown retail, helping keep shopping local and walkable.
Shops, Services, and Openings Coming Soon
Several additional businesses are officially listed as coming soon in Littleton.

Downtown, Diamond Reserve is preparing to open on West Main Street, adding a jewelry retailer to the historic core. Rhonda Allison , a professional skincare brand, is also slated to open a location on South Prince Street, expanding service-oriented retail options downtown.
Coffee service will expand further with 7 Brew Coffee , coming to West Mineral Avenue. The drive-thru-focused concept will add a quick coffee option to the south end of the city.

The financial sector is expanding as well. Academy Bank opened a Downtown Littleton branch in fall 2025. Central Bank (2516 W. Main St.) and Huntington National Bank (100 E. Mineral Ave.) are also officially listed as coming soon, increasing access to banking services near downtown and the Mineral corridor.

A Costco warehouse store will anchor Mineral Place, marking Littleton’s first Costco location. The 159,000-square-foot store will include a gas station and tire center and is projected to open in 2026.

Beyond the anchors, Mineral Place plans include a second big-box retailer yet to be announced and nine smaller retail and dining spaces. A 370-unit luxury apartment community developed by Embrey, known as The Sullivan , will also be part of the project.

As 2026 continues, Littleton’s growth is unfolding on multiple levels. New fitness studios are opening. Restaurants and coffee shops are becoming part of daily routines. Downtown retail is filling in. Major developments like Mineral Place are laying the groundwork for what comes next.

When I surveyed readers this summer about what they wanted more of, restaurant and opening news won by a mile. So this page is the running answer: what's newly open around Littleton 80127 and Ken Caryl, what's coming, and what we lost. A lot of it comes out of county permit files before anyone announces a thing, which is how this newsletter found half the entries below. The Friday email gets each one first.

Ziggi's Coffee, 8020 South Sangre de Cristo. The Colorado-grown drive-thru chain opened its Chatfield and Sangre de Cristo corner on August 27, after a spring and summer of construction on that lot. Dirty sodas, protein coffees, and a kids' menu, plus a drive-thru line that will tell you how the zip is voting.

Hotpot Den, 5934 South Kipling Parkway. A family-run, all-you-can-eat hot pot spot in the old Chen's Kitchen space, with house-made broths and the cook-it-yourself table experience. It quietly became one of the zip's most interesting dinner options the day it opened.

Los Dos Potrillos, 10065 West San Juan Way. Back. The family Mexican standby reopened July 9 after a kitchen fire in March kept it dark for four months, and the line on reopening day said everything about how much this one was missed.
Coming soon

The Summit Steak Bar, the Bevy's building on South Alkire. The steakhouse finally put a date on its banner: opening Monday, August 31, with dinner from 4 and reservations through its site. Months of "live website, no date" end Monday.
Jersey Mike's, 7735 West Long Drive. One zip over, about a mile east of Kipling. The July tenant permit reads like a sub shop starter kit, two kitchen hoods and a brand-new grease trap.

Turnbuckle Distilling, northwest corner of Bowles and C-470. The most ambitious of the batch: a five-acre distillery with a chef-driven restaurant, a silo tasting room, and a working farm on the old Whistling Hare property. Its own site still says Coming Soon with no date.
